conclusion: The product route is closed, and closed by proof rather than by failure to find a bound: k >= log P / max_p (e_p log p) is exactly its strength, and two gcd-1 adversarial families cap that quantity at 1+o(1) for counting/range/residue estimates and at 2+o(1) once gcd normalisation and the one-step recursion on multiples of p are added. The separate smooth-counting lane is also capped, at k >= log n / loglog(2X), which exceeds Erdos-Turan's log_2 n only if the largest element X is below e^2.
confidence: High on the negative results, which are short elementary proofs with explicit witnesses and numerics agreeing with the predicted limits (Omega' measured B=1.041 against limit n/(n-2)=1.0345; Omega measured B=2.125 against limit 2). Lower on P5b, the large-sieve sparsity bound n = O(sqrt(X) log X): the derivation is standard but its normalisation was not independently re-checked in this run, and it is the one claim here I would want a second pair of eyes on. The audit finding against r_186989's loose thread 3 is certain: an explicit infinite family refutes the suggested first step.

threads.what: A weighted or subset product, prod over a chosen graph E of (a+b), instead of all pairs
threads.why_it_might_matter: It is the only door Theorem 4 does not already cover: both adversarial families concentrate their prime mass on a specific pair structure that a chosen E could avoid. The trade is mass-concentration against the size of log P, which falls with |E|.
threads.first_step: For the antipodal family Omega, compute max_E B over E = the complement of the cross-pairs, and see whether B exceeds 2 by a margin that survives the adversary re-optimising p and m.

threads.what: Is X bounded in terms of (n,k) after gcd normalisation?
threads.why_it_might_matter: It is the pivot of the entire sieve and smooth-counting lane: every estimate there is stated in X and is vacuous without a bound on it. Only n=2 examples with unbounded X are known here.
threads.first_step: Search for gcd-1 valid sets with n=3 and X large for S={2,3} and S={2,3,5}: exhaust X up to 10^7 and see whether the witnesses stay below 50 as r_186989 observed, or whether a sporadic large one exists.

threads.what: The occupancy lemma constrains A to a sum-free class structure modulo every prime outside S
threads.why_it_might_matter: It is the only structural constraint found here that does not mention X, before the large sieve reintroduces X. Something that exploits the occupancy pattern across many q jointly, rather than through a sieve inequality, would be in a new information class.
threads.first_step: Measure, on the seven known witnesses, whether the occupied class sets mod q outside S are near-extremal (close to (q+1)/2 classes) or far from it. If they are far from extremal, the sieve is losing most of its available strength.

core_candidates.what: A reusable 'method ceiling' probe: given a proposed bound of the form target >= F(A) over a hypothesis class, search a parameterised adversarial family for the supremum of F, and report the ceiling before anyone spends a run trying to prove the bound
core_candidates.why_reusable: This run's whole value came from computing that ceiling in a few minutes rather than attempting the bound. Any hunt that proposes an inequality assembled from an identity plus a max, which is common, can be pre-screened the same way.
